records.source: וְהָ֣אָדָ֔ם יָדַ֖ע אֶת־חַוָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וַתַּ֨הַר֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד אֶת־קַ֔יִן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר קָנִ֥יתִי אִ֖ישׁ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And the man knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain, and she said, I have gotten a man with YHWH.
pieces: The man was intimate with his wife Eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. She said, "With the help of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I have brought a man into being."

L.1: And the man knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain, and she said, "I have gotten a man with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.1: The man and his wife Eve had a child together. She became pregnant and gave birth to a son named Cain. She said, "With {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s help, I have had a baby boy."

decisions.choice: knew: had sexual relations with
decisions.reason: "Know" is a Hebrew way of speaking of sexual union (4:17, 25; 1 Samuel 1:19). It is a personal word, not a crude one.

decisions.choice: Cain ... I have gotten: the name sounds like the verb
decisions.reason: Eve explains the name Cain (qayin) by the verb she uses, "I have gotten" or "I have made" (qaniti). The verb can mean to acquire and also to create (Proverbs 8:22; Deuteronomy 32:6).

decisions.choice: a man with the LORD: with the LORD's help
alternatives: a man, as the LORD did
decisions.reason: The small word "with" (et) can also mark an object, and some have read "I have gotten a man: the LORD", as if Eve thought her son was the promised one of 3:15. But "with" is its usual sense in such a phrase, and the ancient translations read it as help from God. Eve speaks of her son as "a man", a proud word for a newborn, and she names the LORD as the giver of life.

decisions.choice: was intimate with (B); had a child together (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom "knew" (m1); Balanced and Readable say what it means.

records.heading: Cain and Abel

records.source: וַתֹּ֣סֶף לָלֶ֔דֶת אֶת־אָחִ֖יו אֶת־הָ֑בֶל וַֽיְהִי־הֶ֨בֶל֙ רֹ֣עֵה צֹ֔אן וְקַ֕יִן הָיָ֖ה עֹבֵ֥ד אֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And she added to bear his brother, Abel. And Abel was a shepherd of flock, and Cain was a worker of ground.
pieces: Later she gave birth to his brother Abel. Abel kept flocks of sheep and goats, and Cain worked the ground.

L.2: And again she bore his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, and Cain was a worker of the ground.

R.2: Later she had another son, Abel. Abel took care of sheep and goats, and Cain was a farmer.

decisions.choice: Abel (Hevel): a name that means "breath"
decisions.reason: The name is the word for breath or vapor, something that does not last; Ecclesiastes uses it for what is fleeting (Ecclesiastes 1:2). The story gives no explanation of the name, but Abel's life is short.

decisions.choice: keeper of the flock, worker of the ground: the two main ways of life
decisions.reason: The brothers take up the two callings of the ancient world: herding animals and farming. Cain's work is the man's work of 2:15 and 3:23. The text does not favor one way of life over the other.

decisions.choice: flock: sheep and goats together
decisions.reason: The word covers small livestock, both sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: again she bore
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "she added to bear", a common way of saying "she did it again".

records.source: וַֽיְהִ֖י מִקֵּ֣ץ יָמִ֑ים וַיָּבֵ֨א קַ֜יִן מִפְּרִ֧י הָֽאֲדָמָ֛ה מִנְחָ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was from [the] end of days, and brought Cain from [the] fruit of the ground an offering to YHWH.
pieces: In the course of time Cain brought some of the produce of the ground as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.3: And it happened at the end of days that Cain brought some of the fruit of the ground as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.3: After some time, Cain brought some of his crops as a gift to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: at the end of days: after some time
alternatives: at the end of the year
decisions.reason: The phrase usually means after a period of time, perhaps at the end of a season or a year, when crops were gathered.

decisions.choice: offering: a gift brought to God
alternatives: grain offering (in its later sense only)
decisions.reason: The word means a gift, and it is used for tribute to a king (32:13) as well as for gifts to God. In the laws of Leviticus it names the grain offering; here it is used of both brothers' gifts, plants and animals alike.

records.source: וְהֶ֨בֶל הֵבִ֥יא גַם־ה֛וּא מִבְּכֹר֥וֹת צֹאנ֖וֹ וּמֵֽחֶלְבֵהֶ֑ן וַיִּ֣שַׁע יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־הֶ֖בֶל וְאֶל־מִנְחָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And Abel brought, also he, from [the] firstborn of his flock and from their fat [portions]. And looked YHWH to Abel and to his offering,
pieces: And Abel also brought an offering: some of the firstborn of his flock, with their fat portions. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} looked with favor on Abel and his offering,

L.4: And Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of their fat portions. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looked with favor on Abel and on his offering,

R.4: Abel also brought a gift. He chose some of the first lambs born in his flock and offered their best parts. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was pleased with Abel and his gift,

decisions.choice: the firstborn of his flock and their fat: the first and the best
decisions.reason: The firstborn of the flock and the fat portions were counted as the best and as belonging to God (Exodus 13:12; Leviticus 3:16). Abel's gift is described with care; Cain's simply as "some of the fruit" (verse 3), not the first fruits.

decisions.choice: looked with favor: accepted
decisions.reason: The verb means to look at, here with favor. The story does not say how Cain and Abel knew which offering was accepted.

decisions.choice: their best parts
decisions.reason: Readable says what the fat portions stood for (m1): the best of the animal.

records.source: וְאֶל־קַ֥יִן וְאֶל־מִנְחָת֖וֹ לֹ֣א שָׁעָ֑ה וַיִּ֤חַר לְקַ֨יִן֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ פָּנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: but to Cain and to his offering he did not look. And it burned to Cain greatly, and his face fell.
pieces: but on Cain and his offering {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not look with favor. So Cain was very angry, and his face was downcast.

L.5: but on Cain and on his offering {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not look with favor. And Cain was very angry, and his face fell.

R.5: but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not pleased with Cain and his gift. Cain became very angry, and he looked upset.

decisions.choice: Cain's offering not accepted: the reason is not stated
alternatives: because grain was the wrong kind of offering
because Cain's heart was not right
decisions.reason: The text does not say why. It describes Abel's gift as the first and best (verse 4) and Cain's more plainly, and it says God looked on Abel and Cain themselves as well as on their gifts. Hebrews 11:4 says Abel offered "by faith", and 1 John 3:12 that Cain's own deeds were evil. Grain offerings were acceptable in Israel's law, so the kind of gift is not likely the reason.

decisions.choice: it burned to Cain: Cain was furious
decisions.reason: Anger is described as burning in Hebrew. "His face fell" pictures sullen anger or dejection.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־קָ֑יִן לָ֚מָּה חָ֣רָה לָ֔ךְ וְלָ֖מָּה נָפְל֥וּ פָנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And said YHWH to Cain, why does it burn to you, and why has fallen your face?
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Cain, "Why are you angry? Why is your face downcast?

L.6: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Cain, "Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen?

R.6: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Cain, "Why are you angry? Why do you look so upset?

decisions.choice: why ...? why ...?: God speaks to Cain before he acts
decisions.reason: As with the man and woman in chapter 3, God speaks with Cain by asking questions. This time he speaks before the wrong is done, to warn him (verse 7).

records.source: הֲל֤וֹא אִם־תֵּיטִיב֙ שְׂאֵ֔ת וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א תֵיטִ֔יב לַפֶּ֖תַח חַטָּ֣את רֹבֵ֑ץ וְאֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ תְּשׁ֣וּקָת֔וֹ וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּמְשָׁל־בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Is [it] not, if you do well, lifting up? And if you do not do well, at the door sin [is] crouching, and to you [is] its desire, and you, you must rule over it.
pieces: If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at your door. It wants to have you, but you must master it."

L.7: If you do well, [will there] not [be] lifting up? And if you do not do well, sin [is] crouching at the door, and its desire [is] for you, but you must rule over it."

R.7: If you do what is right, I will accept you. But if you do not do what is right, sin is waiting to attack you, like an animal crouching by the door. Sin wants to control you, but you must control it."

decisions.choice: lifting up: being accepted, with your face lifted up
decisions.reason: "Lifting up" answers "your face has fallen" (verse 6): if Cain does well, his face will be lifted, he will be accepted and at peace. The same word can be used for lifting away guilt (forgiveness), which may also be in view.

decisions.choice: sin is crouching at the door: sin is pictured like an animal lying in wait
alternatives: a sin offering lies at the door
decisions.reason: Sin is pictured as a beast crouching at the entrance, ready to spring. The verb is used for animals lying down (29:2; 49:9). Here, for the first time in the Bible, the word "sin" appears.

decisions.choice: its desire is for you, but you must rule over it: the words of 3:16
alternatives: its desire is for you, and you will rule over it (a promise)
decisions.reason: The words repeat 3:16 ("your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you"). Here sin wants to master Cain, and he is called to master it. The verb form can be a command ("you must") or a promise ("you will"); in the warning, a command or a call fits best.

decisions.choice: like an animal crouching by the door
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of the crouching beast and says what it means (m2).

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר קַ֖יִן אֶל־הֶ֣בֶל אָחִ֑יו וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּהְיוֹתָ֣ם בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיָּ֥קָם קַ֛יִן אֶל־הֶ֥בֶל אָחִ֖יו וַיַּהַרְגֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Cain to Abel his brother. And it was, when they were in the field, and rose up Cain against Abel his brother and killed him.
pieces: Cain spoke to his brother Abel. And while they were in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him.

L.8: And Cain said to Abel his brother ... And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him.

R.8: Cain spoke to his brother Abel. While they were out in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him.

decisions.choice: Cain said to Abel his brother: the Hebrew text gives no words
alternatives: Cain said to Abel his brother, Let us go out to the field (Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, Syriac, Latin)
decisions.reason: The verb "said" normally introduces words, but in the Hebrew text nothing follows. The Samaritan Pentateuch, the Septuagint, the Syriac and the Latin have "Let us go out to the field", which may have dropped out of the Hebrew. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: rose up against his brother and killed him: the first murder
decisions.reason: "Brother" is repeated through the chapter (seven times in verses 2-11): the first murder is the killing of a brother. Jesus speaks of "the blood of righteous Abel" (Matthew 23:35), and 1 John 3:12 warns not to be like Cain.

decisions.choice: Cain said to Abel his brother ...
decisions.reason: Literal marks the gap in the Hebrew text with an ellipsis (m1).

decisions.choice: Cain spoke to his brother Abel
alternatives: Cain said to his brother Abel
decisions.reason: Since the Hebrew gives no words (m1), Balanced and Readable say "spoke to", which needs none.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־קַ֔יִן אֵ֖י הֶ֣בֶל אָחִ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי הֲשֹׁמֵ֥ר אָחִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי׃
records.gloss: And said YHWH to Cain, where [is] Abel your brother? And he said, I do not know; [the] keeper of my brother [am] I?
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" "I do not know," he answered. "Am I my brother's keeper?"

L.9: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Cain, "Where [is] Abel your brother?" And he said, "I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?"

R.9: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} asked Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" Cain answered, "I do not know. Is it my job to take care of my brother?"

decisions.choice: where is Abel your brother?: God's question echoes "where are you?" (3:9)
decisions.reason: As God asked the man "where are you?", he asks Cain about his brother, giving him the chance to confess. Cain answers with a lie and a question.

decisions.choice: my brother's keeper: one who watches over him
decisions.reason: "Keeper" is from the verb "keep" in 2:15, used for the man's care of the garden. Cain's question rejects any duty toward his brother.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתָ ק֚וֹל דְּמֵ֣י אָחִ֔יךָ צֹעֲקִ֥ים אֵלַ֖י מִן־הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said, what have you done? [The] voice of [the] bloods of your brother [is] crying to me from the ground.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "What have you done? Listen! Your brother's blood is crying out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from the ground.

L.10: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood is crying out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from the ground.

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "What have you done? Your brother's blood is calling out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from the ground, asking for justice.

decisions.choice: the voice of your brother's blood is crying out: the murdered man's blood calls for justice
decisions.reason: "Blood" is plural here, as often for shed blood. The verb is used for the cry of the oppressed for help and justice (Exodus 3:7; 22:23). The blood itself cries out from the ground; Hebrews 12:24 contrasts it with the blood of Jesus, "which speaks a better word".

decisions.choice: The LORD said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, the LORD of verse 9; Literal keeps "he".

decisions.choice: Listen!
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "the voice of" into a call to hear, as the Hebrew word can mean ("Hark!").

decisions.choice: asking for justice
decisions.reason: Readable says what the blood's cry is for (m1).

records.source: וְעַתָּ֖ה אָר֣וּר אָ֑תָּה מִן־הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּצְתָ֣ה אֶת־פִּ֔יהָ לָקַ֛חַת אֶת־דְּמֵ֥י אָחִ֖יךָ מִיָּדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And now cursed [are] you from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive the bloods of your brother from your hand.
pieces: Now you are cursed, driven from the ground that opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.

L.11: And now you [are] cursed from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.

R.11: Now you are under a curse, and the ground will no longer be your home. It opened up to soak in your brother's blood, which you spilled.

decisions.choice: cursed from the ground: cursed, and driven away from it
decisions.reason: "From" can mean "away from": Cain will be cut off from the ground he worked (verse 12) and driven from it (verse 14). In 3:17 the ground was cursed; now Cain himself is cursed, the first human being to be cursed.

decisions.choice: the ground opened its mouth: the earth drank the blood
decisions.reason: The ground is pictured as a mouth that took in Abel's blood, and so is a witness to the crime.

records.source: כִּ֤י תַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה לֹֽא־תֹסֵ֥ף תֵּת־כֹּחָ֖הּ לָ֑ךְ נָ֥ע וָנָ֖ד תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה בָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: When you work the ground, it will not again give its strength to you. A wanderer and a fugitive you will be on the earth.
pieces: When you work the ground, it will no longer yield its crops for you. You will be a restless wanderer on the earth."

L.12: When you work the ground, it will no longer give its strength to you; you will be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth."

R.12: When you farm the land, it will not grow good crops for you anymore. You will wander from place to place, with no home on earth."

decisions.choice: its strength: its produce
decisions.reason: The ground's "strength" is what it produces. For a farmer like Cain, this is the end of his work.

decisions.choice: a wanderer and a fugitive: restless, without a settled home
decisions.reason: The two words sound alike (na wa-nad) and together mean someone always on the move, without rest or home. The second returns in the name of the land Cain goes to, Nod (verse 16).

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר קַ֖יִן אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל עֲוֺנִ֖י מִנְּשֹֽׂא׃
records.gloss: And said Cain to YHWH, great [is] my punishment from bearing.
pieces: Cain said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "My punishment is more than I can bear.

L.13: And Cain said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "My punishment [is] too great to bear.

R.13: Cain said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "This punishment is too much for me to bear.

decisions.choice: my punishment is too great to bear
alternatives: my guilt is too great to be forgiven
decisions.reason: The word means both guilt and the punishment that guilt brings, and the verb "bear" can also mean "take away" (forgive). So the line can be read as "my guilt is too great to be forgiven". Cain's next words (verse 14) complain of what will happen to him, which favors "punishment".

records.source: הֵן֩ גֵּרַ֨שְׁתָּ אֹתִ֜י הַיּ֗וֹם מֵעַל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה וּמִפָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶסָּתֵ֑ר וְהָיִ֜יתִי נָ֤ע וָנָד֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ וְהָיָ֥ה כָל־מֹצְאִ֖י יַֽהַרְגֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Behold, you have driven me today from on [the] face of the ground, and from your face I will be hidden, and I will be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth, and it will be [that] everyone who finds me will kill me.
pieces: Today {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are driving me from the land, and I will be hidden from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence. I will be a restless wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."

L.14: Look, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have driven me today from the face of the ground, and from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face I will be hidden; and I will be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."

R.14: Today {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are sending me away from my land, and I will not be near {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} anymore. I will wander from place to place, and anyone who finds me will kill me."

decisions.choice: hidden from your face: shut out of God's presence
decisions.reason: To be hidden from God's face is to lose his care and protection (Deuteronomy 31:17-18; Psalm 27:9). Cain sees that being driven from the land means being driven from God.

decisions.choice: whoever finds me will kill me: other people are assumed
decisions.reason: The story assumes there are other people who might avenge Abel. It does not say who they are; the account follows one family line and says elsewhere that Adam had other sons and daughters (5:4).

decisions.choice: you, your (lowercase by default; You, Your with the setting)
decisions.reason: Cain speaks to God, so "you" and "your" take the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה לָכֵן֙ כָּל־הֹרֵ֣ג קַ֔יִן שִׁבְעָתַ֖יִם יֻקָּ֑ם וַיָּ֨שֶׂם יְהוָ֤ה לְקַ֨יִן֙ א֔וֹת לְבִלְתִּ֥י הַכּוֹת־אֹת֖וֹ כָּל־מֹצְאֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said to him YHWH, therefore anyone who kills Cain, sevenfold he will be avenged. And set YHWH for Cain a sign, so that anyone finding him would not strike him.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Because of this, whoever kills Cain will suffer vengeance seven times over." Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him.

L.15: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Therefore whoever kills Cain, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold." And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} set a sign for Cain, so that no one who found him would strike him.

R.15: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Because of that, if anyone kills Cain, I will punish that person seven times as much." So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put a mark on Cain to warn anyone who found him not to kill him.

decisions.choice: therefore, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "therefore" (laken); the Septuagint, the Syriac and the Latin read "not so" (lo ken), which differs by one letter and answers Cain's fear more directly. The Hebrew text is followed here: because Cain fears for his life, God protects him.

decisions.choice: sevenfold: in full measure
decisions.reason: Seven is a number of completeness. Vengeance "sevenfold" means full and severe vengeance. God's protection limits violence instead of letting it run on, though Lamech will boast of more (verse 24).

decisions.choice: a sign: a mark or token that protected Cain
alternatives: a sign given to Cain to reassure him
decisions.reason: The word means a sign or token (9:12; Exodus 12:13). The text does not say what it was or whether it was on Cain's body; it served to protect him.

decisions.choice: Because of this (B); Because of that (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "because of this" to tie God's answer to Cain's fear (m1).

records.source: וַיֵּ֥צֵא קַ֖יִן מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ־נ֖וֹד קִדְמַת־עֵֽדֶן׃
records.gloss: And went out Cain from before YHWH and dwelt in [the] land of Nod, east of Eden.
pieces: So Cain went out from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s presence and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

L.16: And Cain went out from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

R.16: So Cain left the place where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was near and went to live in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

decisions.choice: Nod: "wandering"
decisions.reason: The name sounds like the word for "fugitive" in verses 12 and 14: Cain settles in the Land of Wandering. No place of that name is known.

decisions.choice: east of Eden: further from the garden
decisions.reason: The man and the woman were sent out to the east of the garden (3:24); Cain goes further east still. Later in Genesis, going east marks moving away from God's blessing (11:2; 13:11).

records.source: וַיֵּ֤דַע קַ֨יִן֙ אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד אֶת־חֲנ֑וֹךְ וַֽיְהִי֙ בֹּ֣נֶה עִ֔יר וַיִּקְרָא֙ שֵׁ֣ם הָעִ֔יר כְּשֵׁ֖ם בְּנ֥וֹ חֲנֽוֹךְ׃
records.gloss: And knew Cain his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch. And he was building a city, and he called the name of the city according to the name of his son, Enoch.
pieces: Cain was intimate with his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. Cain was building a city, and he named it Enoch, after his son.

L.17: And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch. And he was building a city, and he called the name of the city after the name of his son, Enoch.

R.17: Cain and his wife had a son named Enoch. Cain was building a city at that time, and he named it Enoch, after his son.

decisions.choice: his wife: not explained
decisions.reason: The story does not say who Cain's wife was. Adam had other sons and daughters (5:4), and in the first generations marriage within the family is assumed.

decisions.choice: he was building a city: Cain, or possibly Enoch
alternatives: Enoch was building a city, named after his son Irad
decisions.reason: The natural reading is that Cain built the city and named it after his son. Some read Enoch as the builder, which would explain the unusual wording "according to the name of his son".

decisions.choice: a city: the wanderer builds a settled place
decisions.reason: Cain was sentenced to wander, yet he builds a city, the first in the Bible. The line of Cain goes on to found the arts of civilization (verses 20-22).

records.source: וַיִּוָּלֵ֤ד לַֽחֲנוֹךְ֙ אֶת־עִירָ֔ד וְעִירָ֕ד יָלַ֖ד אֶת־מְחֽוּיָאֵ֑ל וּמְחִיּיָאֵ֗ל יָלַד֙ אֶת־מְת֣וּשָׁאֵ֔ל וּמְתוּשָׁאֵ֖ל יָלַ֥ד אֶת־לָֽמֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And was born to Enoch Irad, and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehijael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
pieces: Enoch had a son named Irad, Irad was the father of Mehujael, Mehujael was the father of Methushael, and Methushael was the father of Lamech.

L.18: And to Enoch was born Irad, and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.

R.18: Enoch had a son named Irad. Irad was the father of Mehujael. Mehujael was the father of Methushael. Methushael was the father of Lamech.

decisions.choice: Mehujael: the name is spelled two ways in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew writes the name Mehujael the first time and Mehijael the second. Translations use one form; the meaning is not affected.

decisions.choice: Lamech: not the Lamech of 5:25-31
decisions.reason: This Lamech, of Cain's line, is not the father of Noah in Seth's line (5:28-29). Some names in the two lines are alike (Enoch, Lamech; Irad and Jared; Methushael and Methuselah).

records.source: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֥וֹ לֶ֖מֶךְ שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשִׁ֑ים שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאַחַת֙ עָדָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית צִלָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And took for himself Lamech two wives; [the] name of the one [was] Adah, and [the] name of the second [was] Zillah.
pieces: Lamech married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.

L.19: And Lamech took for himself two wives; the name of the one [was] Adah, and the name of the second [was] Zillah.

R.19: Lamech married two women. One was named Adah, and the other was named Zillah.

decisions.choice: two wives: the first time a man marries more than one woman
decisions.reason: Lamech is the first man in the Bible to have two wives, a departure from the one flesh of 2:24. The text reports it without comment, but the story of Lamech that follows is one of pride and violence.

records.source: וַתֵּ֥לֶד עָדָ֖ה אֶת־יָבָ֑ל ה֣וּא הָיָ֔ה אֲבִ֕י יֹשֵׁ֥ב אֹ֖הֶל וּמִקְנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And bore Adah Jabal; he was [the] father of dwellers [in] tent and livestock.
pieces: Adah gave birth to Jabal. He was the father of those who live in tents and raise livestock.

L.20: And Adah bore Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and [have] livestock.

R.20: Adah had a son named Jabal. He was the first of the people who live in tents and raise animals.

decisions.choice: father of: the founder of a way of life
decisions.reason: "Father" here means the first of a group or the founder of a craft, not only an ancestor (as in 2 Kings 2:12 of the prophets' leader).

records.source: וְשֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו יוּבָ֑ל ה֣וּא הָיָ֔ה אֲבִ֕י כָּל־תֹּפֵ֥שׂ כִּנּ֖וֹר וְעוּגָֽב׃
records.gloss: And [the] name of his brother [was] Jubal; he was [the] father of everyone who plays lyre and pipe.
pieces: His brother's name was Jubal. He was the father of all who play the lyre and the flute.

L.21: And the name of his brother [was] Jubal; he was the father of all who play the lyre and the pipe.

R.21: His brother was named Jubal. He was the first of all the people who play music on harps and flutes.

decisions.choice: lyre and pipe: a stringed and a wind instrument
decisions.reason: The first is a lyre, a small handheld stringed instrument (David's "harp", 1 Samuel 16:23). The second is probably a pipe or flute. Together they stand for all music.

records.source: וְצִלָּ֣ה גַם־הִ֗וא יָֽלְדָה֙ אֶת־תּ֣וּבַל קַ֔יִן לֹטֵ֕שׁ כָּל־חֹרֵ֥שׁ נְחֹ֖שֶׁת וּבַרְזֶ֑ל וַֽאֲח֥וֹת תּֽוּבַל־קַ֖יִן נַֽעֲמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And Zillah, also she bore Tubal-cain, a forger of every cutting [tool] of bronze and iron. And [the] sister of Tubal-cain [was] Naamah.
pieces: Zillah also had a son, Tubal-cain, who forged all kinds of tools out of bronze and iron. Tubal-cain's sister was Naamah.

L.22: And Zillah also bore Tubal-cain, a forger of every tool of bronze and iron; and the sister of Tubal-cain [was] Naamah.

R.22: Zillah also had a son, Tubal-cain. He made all kinds of tools out of bronze and iron. Tubal-cain had a sister named Naamah.

decisions.choice: a forger of every tool of bronze and iron: a metalworker
alternatives: a sharpener of every cutting tool
decisions.reason: The words mean one who hammers or sharpens metal and one who works it. Bronze and iron stand for metal working in general; the account names the first of the crafts without fixing a date for them.

decisions.choice: Naamah: named without a story
decisions.reason: Naamah ("pleasant") is one of the few women named in these genealogies. Nothing more is told of her.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לֶ֜מֶךְ לְנָשָׁ֗יו עָדָ֤ה וְצִלָּה֙ שְׁמַ֣עַן קוֹלִ֔י נְשֵׁ֣י לֶ֔מֶךְ הַאְזֵ֖נָּה אִמְרָתִ֑י כִּ֣י אִ֤ישׁ הָרַ֨גְתִּי֙ לְפִצְעִ֔י וְיֶ֖לֶד לְחַבֻּרָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Lamech to his wives, Adah and Zillah, hear my voice, wives of Lamech, give ear to my word: for a man I have killed for my wound, and a young man for my bruise.
pieces: Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, listen to me; wives of Lamech, hear my words: I have killed a man for wounding me, a young man for striking me.

L.23: And Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my word: for I have killed a man for wounding me, and a young man for striking me.

R.23: Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, listen to me! Wives of Lamech, hear what I say! A man hurt me, so I killed him. A young man struck me, so I killed him.

decisions.choice: Lamech's song: the first poem of a human after the garden is a boast
decisions.reason: The verse is poetry, in pairs of lines that say the same thing twice. Where the man's first words were joy at the woman (2:23), Lamech's are a boast of revenge.

decisions.choice: I have killed a man for wounding me: an act already done
alternatives: I will kill any man who wounds me (a threat)
decisions.reason: The verb has a completed form and most likely reports a killing. Some read it as a threat. Either way, Lamech takes a life for a wound: vengeance far beyond the harm.

decisions.choice: a man ... a young man: one victim, described twice
decisions.reason: In Hebrew poetry the second line usually repeats the first in other words, so "a man" and "a young man" are probably the same person.

records.source: כִּ֥י שִׁבְעָתַ֖יִם יֻקַּם־קָ֑יִן וְלֶ֖מֶךְ שִׁבְעִ֥ים וְשִׁבְעָֽה׃
records.gloss: For sevenfold Cain will be avenged, and Lamech seventy and seven.
pieces: If Cain is avenged seven times, then Lamech seventy-seven times!"

L.24: If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold."

R.24: If anyone who kills Cain will be punished seven times as much, then anyone who hurts me will be punished seventy-seven times as much!"

decisions.choice: seventy-seven: unlimited vengeance, reversed by Jesus
decisions.reason: Lamech turns God's protection of Cain (verse 15) into a boast of endless revenge. Jesus reverses the number when he tells Peter to forgive "seventy-seven times" (Matthew 18:22, where the Greek can also be read "seventy times seven").

decisions.choice: If ... then
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word can mean "for" or "if"; English reads the comparison more clearly with "if ... then".

records.source: וַיֵּ֨דַע אָדָ֥ם עוֹד֙ אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ שֵׁ֑ת כִּ֣י שָֽׁת־לִ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ זֶ֣רַע אַחֵ֔ר תַּ֣חַת הֶ֔בֶל כִּ֥י הֲרָג֖וֹ קָֽיִן׃
records.gloss: And knew Adam again his wife, and she bore a son and called his name Seth, for has appointed to me God another offspring in place of Abel, for Cain killed him.
pieces: Adam was intimate with his wife again, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, "God has given me another child in place of Abel, since Cain killed him."

L.25: And Adam knew his wife again, and she bore a son and called his name Seth, "For God has appointed for me another offspring in place of Abel, because Cain killed him."

R.25: Adam and his wife had another son. She named him Seth. She said, "God has given me another child to take the place of Abel, because Cain killed him."

decisions.choice: Adam: here a personal name
decisions.reason: The word that meant "the man" or "humankind" is used here without the article, plainly as a name. From here on the first man is called Adam (5:1-5).

decisions.choice: Seth: a name that sounds like "appointed"
decisions.reason: Eve explains the name Seth (shet) by the verb shat, "he has appointed" or "granted".

decisions.choice: another offspring: the line continues after Abel's death
decisions.reason: The word is "seed", the word of 3:15. Through Seth the line of promise goes on, the line Genesis 5 follows to Noah.

decisions.choice: "For God has appointed for me ..."
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say "she said"; Literal puts Eve's words in quotation marks after "For", as her reason for the name.

records.source: וּלְשֵׁ֤ת גַּם־הוּא֙ יֻלַּד־בֵּ֔ן וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ אֱנ֑וֹשׁ אָ֣ז הוּחַ֔ל לִקְרֹ֖א בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And to Seth, also to him was born a son, and he called his name Enosh. Then it was begun to call on [the] name of YHWH.
pieces: Seth also had a son, and he named him Enosh. At that time people began to call on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.26: And to Seth also a son was born, and he called his name Enosh. Then [people] began to call on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.26: Seth also had a son, and he named him Enosh. That was when people began to pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and worship him by name.

decisions.choice: Enosh: a word for a human being
decisions.reason: Enosh is a poetic word for a human being, often stressing frailty (Psalm 8:5; 103:15).

decisions.choice: to call on the name of the LORD: to worship him and pray to him
decisions.reason: To call on the LORD's name is to worship and pray to him (12:8; Psalm 116:17). In contrast with the line of Cain, the line of Seth turns to the LORD. Exodus 6:3 says God made himself known by this name to Moses in a new way; here the narrator uses the name for the worship of the earliest people.

decisions.choice: [people] began
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "it was begun", with no subject; Literal brackets "people".

decisions.choice: pray to the LORD and worship him by name
alternatives: call on the name of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what calling on the LORD's name means (m2).
